1. My true preference is w > x > y > z
2. I have high priority at w (rank 1) and y (rank 1)
3. Most other applicants seem to favor y, which could make y more competitive
4. If I rank y too high, I might get crowded out by other students who also want y
5. By ranking w first, I leverage my top priority status there
6. If I rank y second, I maintain a strategic backup option with high priority
7. Ranking x third keeps my true second preference available
8. z remains least preferred due to lower priority and personal preference

The goal is to maximize my chances of getting my most preferred school while having a robust backup strategy.

The key is balancing my true preferences with strategic positioning and my priority ranks.
